name: Surya Kund Prasad (rice & potato cooked in hot spring)
signature_dish: rice-and-potato prasad cooked in 88°C thermal spring
why_it_matters: Centuries-old ritual unique to Yamunotri — pilgrims tie raw rice or potatoes (with a pinch of salt) in muslin cloth and dip them into Surya Kund's 88°C geothermal pool beside the temple. The bundle cooks in 5-10 minutes, is offered to the deity, and then carried home as blessed prasad. There is no equivalent at any other Char Dham.
insider_tip: Buy the muslin-cloth rice/potato pouch from the small stalls at the temple plaza (₹20-50). Hand the cooked prasad to the priest first for offering, then collect — eating it before the offering breaks the ritual.
signature_address: Surya Kund, Yamunotri Temple complex, Uttarkashi District, Uttarakhand 249141

name: GMVN Tourist Rest House Restaurant
why_it_matters: The state-run Garhwal Mandal Vikas Nigam (GMVN) rest house at Janki Chatti — 7km before Yamunotri — operates the most reliable kitchen on the trek-base side. Menu is whatever the kitchen has cooked that day (dal, rice, roti, one sabzi, paratha-bread for breakfast). Pilgrims with weak stomachs trust GMVN over private dhabas because the hygiene is government-supervised.
insider_tip: Tell the caretaker the night before if you want a 5am breakfast before the trek — they'll have parathas and tea ready. The 'menu' is fictional; eat what the kitchen has cooked.
signature_address: GMVN Tourist Rest House, Janki Chatti, Yamunotri Road, Uttarkashi District, Uttarakhand 249141

name: Champasar Heritage Restaurant
why_it_matters: A roughly 50-year-old family-run heritage homestay on Yamunotri Road — one of the few places in Janki Chatti that cooks Garhwali home food (mandua roti, kafuli, jhangora) instead of generic dal-chawal. Pure-veg, no alcohol, in line with the strict religious bylaw of the Yamunotri precinct.
insider_tip: Non-residents can call ahead (+91 95488 16738) and request lunch or dinner — they'll cook to order if you ask for the Garhwali set, otherwise you get the standard north-Indian thali tourists default to.
signature_address: Champasar Heritage, Janki Chatti, Yamunotri Road, Uttarkashi District, Uttarakhand 249141

name: Trek-route dhabas (Janki Chatti to Yamunotri)
why_it_matters: The 6km uphill trek from Janki Chatti to the temple is dotted with seasonal tarpaulin-and-tin dhabas (open May-Oct) selling hot maggi, parathas, and chai. There are no named brand operators — stalls are run by Garhwali families on rotating GMVN trekking-route licences. Strictly pure-veg, no alcohol, no eggs (religious bylaw extends across the entire trek path).
insider_tip: Carry ₹500 in ₹10-50 notes — most stalls don't accept UPI above Bhairon Mandir (3km mark). Hot lemon-honey-ginger water (₹40-60) is the smartest order at altitude — sugar drinks worsen mild AMS.
signature_address: Trek path between Janki Chatti and Yamunotri Temple, Uttarkashi District, Uttarakhand 249141
